source: Actual lesson renderer at first decision; text overlays removed from scene only. The first authored question is the invitation.

captures.question: Which return should you expect next?
captures.situation: Your wide serves have pulled this returner off the court twice. Watch both returns.

captures.question: How hard do you go at this one?
captures.situation: Their slice lands short and stays low. You come forward to it; they're still deep.

captures.question: Is this the ball to go down the line?
captures.situation: The line is open, but their low crosscourt pulls you wide, and you're late.

captures.question: What does that one winner tell you?
captures.situation: Off a low, neutral ball, you go down the line and clip the paint. Winner.

captures.question: Where do you recover to?
captures.situation: Your deep crosscourt pushes them outside the sideline. You finish balanced.

captures.question: Which target makes them stop and turn?
captures.situation: You have a comfortable short forehand. Watch where the defender is running before you choose.

captures.question: Which shot leaves you less to cover?
captures.situation: A deep ball to your backhand. They're balanced and could go either way.

captures.question: What keeps the lead working for you?
captures.situation: You lead 5–2. Your rally ball has started landing shorter.

captures.question: Where does the rhythm break?
captures.situation: You reach your spot. Watch the split step and your first move.

captures.question: Which approach sets up your volley?
captures.situation: You're balanced on a short forehand. Their recovery leaves the line open.

captures.question: Where does your return go?
captures.situation: A big first serve pulls you wide. The server stays back for their next ball.

captures.question: Where do you meet this ball?
captures.situation: A slower, high ball lands short. You're balanced, with time to move.

captures.question: What's different about the two returns?
captures.situation: Both second serves go in. Watch where the receiver meets each one.

captures.question: What do you change on the next ball?
captures.situation: Your forehand goes into the net. Watch it again, held at the moment you hit it.

captures.question: How do you use the extra time?
captures.situation: Your slice has bought time. Your forehand is your stronger shot.

captures.question: Where do you send this one?
captures.situation: They approach and come in. They stop just inside the service line as you hit.

captures.question: Where does your pass go?
captures.situation: They approach and close in, shading toward your down-the-line side.

captures.question: What do you change on the next ball?
captures.situation: You aim crosscourt, but your forehand flies wide to the right. Watch it again, held at contact.

captures.question: Where do you take it?
captures.situation: Another high, heavy ball comes to your forehand. At the baseline it will kick above your shoulder.

captures.question: How do you break the pattern?
captures.situation: They're 2 m behind their baseline, looping everything back. This one lands short enough to step in on.

captures.question: What do you do with it?
captures.situation: Their angle pulls you off the court. You reach it low and late; they're in the middle.

captures.question: Which first serve makes their return hardest?
captures.situation: First serve from the deuce side. The returner has moved toward the T to protect their backhand.

captures.question: Next ball like this: where do you wait?
captures.situation: They hit big. Their crosscourt forehand is coming into your backhand corner at 125 km/h.

captures.question: Where does your forehand go?
captures.situation: They're left-handed. You've run around your backhand to hit a forehand.

captures.question: Same serve again. Where do you start?
captures.situation: They hit a big first serve, around 185 km/h, down the T.

captures.question: What's your answer?
captures.situation: They drop-shot you and stay mid-court, where they hit it. You get there in time.

captures.question: How do you use that lean?
captures.situation: Their backhand is the weak side, and they've started leaning toward it before you hit.

captures.question: Where does it go?
captures.situation: Their crosscourt lands short. You step in, set, and they're still getting back to the middle.

captures.question: What do you hit?
captures.situation: Their crosscourt pulls you off the court on your forehand side, and you only just get there.

captures.question: Which plan fits this point?
captures.situation: Their reply comes to your forehand. The far side is open.

captures.question: Which plan fits this point?
captures.situation: Their ball takes you towards the sideline. Watch both players.

captures.question: Which plan fits this point?
captures.situation: Their reply lands inside the service line. They remain deep.

captures.question: Where do you serve to set up the point?
captures.situation: 30-30, deuce court. They crowd the middle to protect their backhand.

captures.question: Where does your return go?
captures.situation: 15-40. A slow second serve sits up on your forehand. The server stays back.

captures.question: Which reply fits your position?
captures.situation: Their ball pulls you wide on the forehand side.

captures.question: Which reply fits your position?
captures.situation: Their ball pulls you wide on the backhand side.

captures.question: When do you make room for the forehand?
captures.situation: Their ball is coming to your backhand side. You have time to move around it.

captures.question: How do you prepare for the short ball?
captures.situation: A short ball is coming to your backhand. There is space ahead of you.

captures.question: Where do you get ready for the return?
captures.situation: Your wide serve is on its way. The returner has not struck it yet.

captures.question: What do you do after serving?
captures.situation: Your wide serve is travelling. The returner can still change the next ball.

captures.question: What does this serve give you time for?
captures.situation: A fast serve is coming into your backhand. Your preparation window is small.

captures.question: What can you do with the time available?
captures.situation: This serve arrives more slowly. You can meet it inside the baseline with space to swing.

captures.question: Does this contact support changing direction?
captures.situation: You are pulled wide and behind the baseline on your backhand. The opposite sideline looks inviting.

captures.question: What has changed from the stretched wide ball?
captures.situation: This ball is shorter. You have time to set on the backhand, and they are recovering toward the crosscourt side.

captures.question: What does this low first volley need?
captures.situation: Your approach brings you in. Their passing shot dips below net height on your forehand side.

captures.question: What does the higher contact offer?
captures.situation: Your approach moves them wide. This backhand volley is above the net, with the opposite side open.

captures.question: Can you make their first volley difficult?
captures.situation: They are coming in and covering the obvious passing lane. Your contact is low behind the baseline.

captures.question: Where is the larger space now?
captures.situation: They have closed much nearer the net and cover the passing angles. You have room to lift the ball.

captures.question: What is realistic from this late pickup?
captures.situation: You read the drop late from behind the baseline. You reach it low, still moving forward.

captures.question: What has arriving early made available?
captures.situation: You spot the drop early. You arrive higher and more balanced, while they remain deep near the middle.

captures.question: Your partner is crossing. Where do you move?
captures.situation: You serve. Your partner crosses for the return. For a moment, their old side looks painfully open.

captures.question: Which return uses the space they are giving you?
captures.situation: The net player looks ready to pounce. You still have a crosscourt lane to the server. Don’t let their presence choose your return.

captures.question: Who takes this deep lob?
captures.situation: A deep lob goes over you. Your partner is already deeper. Both of you chasing it would leave nobody organising the next ball.

captures.question: Your partner holds their side. Where do you recover?
captures.situation: Your partner stays near the net. The return is coming towards your side of the baseline.

captures.question: Their net player moves across early. What changes?
captures.situation: As the serve bounces, their net player moves towards the middle.

captures.question: You can reach this lob in balance. Who takes it?
captures.situation: The lob is dropping behind you. Your partner is deeper, and you have time to turn.

captures.question: Where do you serve?
captures.situation: 30-30, deuce court. The returner stands close to the middle to protect their backhand.

captures.question: Where does your return go?
captures.situation: You lead 5–2. Their serve: a big first serve, wide to your forehand.

captures.question: Where does your second serve go?
captures.situation: 30–40. You missed your first serve.

captures.question: Where does your first serve go?
captures.situation: 30–15. The returner has shaded wide to cover your wide serve.

captures.question: Where do you stand to return it?
captures.situation: 30–40, break point. Their big first serve is coming down the T.

captures.question: Where do you stand to return it?
captures.situation: 15–30. Their second serve is a high, heavy kick.

captures.question: Where do you serve?
captures.situation: Your serve. They're standing guard in the middle, ready for it.
